extracted.intended_audience: prospective and appointed NSF SBIR/STTR panelists and mail reviewers (and applicants seeking to understand review expectations)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NSF SBIR/STTR review-process guidance for panelists and mail reviewers describing assignment, required compliance, merit-review criteria (NSB-approved and program-specific technical/commercial criteria), and panelist administrative/COI obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic assignment / relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals received by the NSF SBIR/STTR Program are assigned to appropriate topics where they will be reviewed if they meet NSF proposal preparation requirements and are in compliance with the program announcement, solicitation or Dear Colleague Letter (supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be assigned to the appropriate program topic to be reviewed; topic fit is a gate for review. Ensure the proposal aligns with the assigned topic's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with NSF proposal preparation requirements and program solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will be reviewed only if they meet NSF proposal preparation requirements and are in compliance with the program announcement, solicitation or Dear Colleague Letter (supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that proposals adhere to formatting, content, and submission rules in the solicitation; non-compliant proposals may not proceed to merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum peer review (three experts)
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals are carefully reviewed by a minimum of three experts in the particular fields represented by the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proposal should receive at least three independent expert evaluations selected by Program Directors; reviewers should cover relevant technical/commercial expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit (NSB-approved merit review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF proposals are evaluated through use of the two National Science Board (NSB)-approved merit review criteria: intellectual merit ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the potential to advance knowledge, the creativity and originality of the approach, and the qualifications of the investigators as described by the NSB merit review framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts (NSB-approved merit review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: ... and the broader impacts of the proposed effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the likely benefits to society and contributions to specific, desired societal outcomes (e.g., education, workforce development, public engagement) per NSB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR program-specific critical review criteria (technical and commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of the NSF SBIR/STTR Program, critical additional review criteria are utilized to highlight the specific objectives of the program and to ensure that all proposals are reviewed for both their technical and commercial merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the SBIR/STTR Merit Review Guidelines (Technical/Commercial) to evaluate the project's technical feasibility, commercialization potential, market opportunity, business model, and readiness for follow-on funding or scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Guidelines (technical/commercial) — followable rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit Review Guidelines (Technical/Commercial): The SBIR/STTR merit review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the linked SBIR/STTR technical/commercial review guidelines for specific scoring rubrics, examples, and criteria definitions used to assess both technical merit and commercial potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: These reviewers are selected by Program Directors charged with the oversight of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Directors select reviewers to ensure appropriate expertise and fairness; reviewers should expect oversight and assignment from program staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist Conflict of Interest (COI) and confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Your designation as a NSF panelist requires that you be aware of and sensitive to potential conflicts that may arise during your service. You are also required to maintain the confidentiality of all proposals and applicants. Please review, sign and return the Conflict-of-Interests and Confidentiality Statement for NSF Panelists form to the NSF staff person that invited you to serve on the panel. Put the ‘panel ID’ number in the panel name field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must identify and avoid conflicts, sign the COI/confidentiality statement, keep proposal contents confidential, and provide the panel ID on the form. Failure to disclose COI or maintain confidentiality is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist administrative and procedural requirements (FastLane/IPS, travel, virtual panels)
rubrics_metrics.description: FastLane Instructions for Panelists: How to submit the registration required for every review panel, review assigned proposals, submit reviews, and navigate through the interactive panel system (IPS), which is used during the live panel meeting. FastLane Instructions for Mail Reviewers: Step-by-step instructions for using FastLane to review a proposal and submit a “mail review” electronically to NSF. Travel Instructions for Panelists: Details on compensation rates, federal employees/non-US citizens/non-permanent residents, travel/hotel reservations and payment information. Virtual Panels: Guides and guidelines for the virtual panel review process in the Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists must complete FastLane/IPS registration, follow system procedures to access and submit reviews, follow travel/payment rules if attending in person, and follow virtual-panel guidance when applicable. These administrative steps are required for participation and submission of reviews.
